podcast.title: Demo Version
podcast.body: A demo version of the title track "Parklife" was recorded in 1993, before actor Phil Daniels was hired to perform the spoken word parts in the verses. In this early stage, Damon Albarn performed those speaking bits himself. Blur "graciously made that version available to their fans via their official website." "Blur with the demo version of Parklife recorded in 1993 before they hired actor Phil Daniels to do the speaking parts in the verses."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: A track from the *Park Life* album, featuring guest vocalist actor Phil Daniels (who starred as Jimmy in The Who's *Quadrophenia* film version). The song is distinctly British-sounding, without disguising the accent and using British idioms like "Dustman." "Now that is a pretty British sounding song."

podcast.body: The title track from their 1994 album "Park Life" featured Cockney bits provided by actor Phil Daniels, known for playing Jimmy the mod in the movie Quadrophenia. This song exemplified the Britishness of their sound. "Blur and the title track over their 1994 album Park Life. The Cockney Bits are courtesy of an actor named Phil Daniels."
